51395009.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to EED (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Figure 2 caption: Fig. 2. Surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensorgrams for compounds 1 (R¹ = H) and 20 (R¹ = NH₂) binding to EED protein. Data was generated using single cycle kinetics, whereby five or nine increasing concentrations of compound serially injected with a single dissociation. Red lines are the binding signal data, black lines are the 1:1 global fit to the data. Concentrations used for single cycle kinetics were 10, 31.6, 100, 316 and 1000 nM for compound 1 and 0.1, 0.316, 1, 3.16, 10, 31.6, 100, 316 and 1000 nM for compound 20.
original_paragraph.Table 1 footnote a: Nanomolar affinity; geometric mean of at least two Kd determinations per compound (unless otherwise stated).
original_paragraph.Table 1 footnote b: Nanomolar affinity predicted by FEP as implemented in the Schrödinger Maestro software suite.
original_paragraph.Table 1 footnote c: Nanomolar PRC2 inhibition determined by measurement of H3K27 trimethylation in G401 cells in a HTRF assay.
original_paragraph.Table 1 footnote d: Measured using shake-flask method with a buffer/octanol volume ratio of 100:1.
original_paragraph.Table 1 footnote e: Human liver microsome intrinsic clearance; μL/min/mg protein.
original_paragraph.Table 1 footnote f: Intrinsic clearance measured for cryopreserved rat hepatocytes; μL/min/×10⁶ cell.
original_paragraph.Table 1 footnote g: Solubility in aqueous phosphate buffer, pH 7.4 after 24 h at 25 °C; μM.
original_paragraph.Table 1 footnote h: Hypothetical compound used in FEP calculations only and not synthesised or tested.
